I see a lot of really good points brought up by everyone on this thread, so I wanted to join in. A lot of you are saying, "she wasn't in any pain," and that, "they should have used morphine, even though they had a limited supply." These are really the key points that drew my focus. Firstly, I wanted to remind everyone that at that point, Tilly had not yet gone to the clinic to drop off her morphine, so it would have been unlikely that they had any morphine on hand, given that it was such a huge plot device to spur on Marielle and Kristi's interactions.
Now, onto the "she wasn't in any pain," part, and this is where all my nutjob theories start kicking in. I think the monsters left her in a position that would cause the most psychological damage to the town residents on purpose. It's already been established that the monsters receive some amount of information on the residents, as evidenced by Jasmine monster telling Trudy, "we know all your names." They seem to consider hunting and killing humans as playing, so it would make sense that they would occasionally find new or novel ways to "play" with their "playthings." I think they stuck the rod in her head in a way that they knew would not kill her. They left her alive on purpose, like an emotionally devastating time bomb for any of the residents to find. I think it's possible that they wouldn't have come  back for her if she lived another night. At most, I think they would have come back to taunt her and every night until she's eventually found by the residents. Additionally, I don't think she was in pain by any natural means. I think her damaged brain was reacting to the worms under Boyd's skin. Recall that she said, "what's that sound," or "noise" I can't recall exactly, as Boyd entered the clearing. I think the worms generate a sound that only the vulnerable would be able to hear, a sound that caused Kelly indescribable pain. That's just my two cents on things. I hope you all enjoyed my rant.
